Title: Meeting of Maori shareholders in the Te Whaiti Nui-A-Toi block on the Murumurunga marae, Te Whaiti, Ureweras.

Date: January 1975

Photographer: G. Reithmaier

Murumurunga marae is located on the edge of Te Urewera, 20 km outside Murupara. The primary hapū are Ngāti Hamua ki Te Whaiti, Ngāti Kohiwi, Ngāti Mahanga, Ngāti Te Au, Ngāti Te Karaha, Ngāti Tuahiwi, Ngāti Whare ki Ngā Potiki and Warahoe ki Te Whaiti of Ngāti Whare.

The whare tipuna is named Wharepakau-tao-tao-ki-te-Kapua. Murumurunga connects ancestrally to the Mātaatua waka, the maunga Tuwatawata and the awa Whirinaki.

ObjectName.value: Onepoto Redoubt on the shore of Lake Waikaremoana, 1874 (27526385843)

Categories.value: Fortifications in New Zealand|Lake Waikaremoana|Flickr images reviewed by FlickreviewR|Images from Archives New Zealand|Te Urewera (geographic area)|Redoubts in New Zealand

ImageDescription.value:
The Onepoto redoubt, Te Upoko-o-Te Ao, was built of stone with earth sods (as shown on the lower left of the image). Constructed in 1871 as part of the campaign against Te Kooti, the redoubt was manned by Armed Constabulary troops until 1877. It guarded the 'frontier' into Te Urewera from the East Coast, and a government boat also patrolled the lake. It was scaled back to a police base from 1878.

The photograph itself comes from a fragile album of New Zealand War memorials, graves and sites. It was created by the War Graves Branch of the Department of Internal Affairs, and includes images from across the country.

Archives Reference: IA76 Box 5/ 29 archway.archives.govt.nz/ViewFullItem.do?code=22252525

ImageDescription.value: Te Mana Motuhakeō Tuhoe patch worn during a protest march in Wellington on 6 February 2024. Ruatoki is a town in the eastern Bay of Plenty. Ngāi Tūhoe is an iwi from the Te Urewera region. This photograph was taken in front of the National War Memorial, Wellington. | Photographed using a Sony fixed-lens compactcamera | Camera timestamp information in UTC | Metadata timestamp 08-Jan-2025 23:25:04 +0000 (UTC) | More background. The Waitangi Solidarity Hīkoi 2024 was organized by the Pōneke Anti-Fascist Coalition and took place in Te Whanganui-a-Tara/Wellington on Waitangi Day on Tuesday 6 February 2024. The protest was directly related to the nascent Treaty Principles Bill legislation, which was formally introduced to the New Zealand parliament later that year in November 2024. If passed into law, the proposed legislation would redefine the principles by which the 1840 Treaty of Waitangi (Te Tiriti)should be interpreted by courts and effectively extinguish the indigenous rights granted in that long-standing agreement.
